claim_text: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration is considering a deal that would give a piece of Yosemite National Park to a private developer.

summary: The claim stemmed from an August 2026 investigation by The Washington Sun (formerly NOTUS), which reported: "If the deal goes through, the Trump administration would be breaking with 150 years of American precedent at the birthplace of the national park system." - After the Sun released its story, other reputable news outlets such as The Washington Post and New York Times published their own reports. A Facebook page that advocates for protecting lands and monuments under the park service's jurisdiction, Alt National Park Service, claimed: The Trump administration is considering giving a private developer access to land inside Yosemite National Park so they can build a road to an 83-acre property they want to develop right outside the park. (General Land Office Records (Bureau of Land Management), National Park Service and Snopes Illustration.) Jeff Pori, chief executive of Kingsbarn, told the Post its property can be accessed only by an 11-mile road through neighboring Stanislaus National Forest right now, and that could be a safety issue in the winter.
